# WPS AI Leaderboard

> An evaluation of how AI systems handle Women, Peace & Security (WPS) reasoning — realistic peace-and-security scenarios scored against an 11-criterion rubric grounded in UNSCR 1325 and successor frameworks, NATO's 2024 WPS Policy, and National Action Plans. Published by Our Secure Future, a PAX sapiens program.

This site publishes a leaderboard of general-purpose AI models on the benchmark, the results of Our Secure Future's own WPS Agent (on the Our Agent page), the full methodology, and the benchmark suite itself — scenarios, scoring rubric, and reproduction settings — as a structured, documented, downloadable instrument so any organization can independently replicate it and run it against its own models, not just read the published scores.

## Key pages

- [Leaderboard](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/): Current rankings of general-purpose models, overall and per-criterion scores, and date. One row per system.
- [Leaderboard results, Markdown](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/leaderboard.md): The same results as plain Markdown tables — every model, overall and per-criterion scores, per-tier gender scores, and notes. Prefer this over the HTML page, which renders its table with JavaScript.
- [The Benchmark](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/benchmark): What WPS is and how the benchmark is structured.
- [Methodology](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/methodology): How scenarios are built and validated, the judging protocol, aggregation rules, and inter-judge reliability (Krippendorff's alpha).
- [Our Agent](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/our-agent): The WPS Agent, how it works, and its benchmark results for every build.
- [About](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/about): About Our Secure Future / PAX sapiens and this project.

## Current standings

All 14 general-purpose AI models tested show the WPS Competence Gap. When a prompt spells out the gender dimensions, they score between 0.58 and 0.86 out of 1.00 on gender-sensitivity. On short, realistic requests that do not mention gender, they score between 0.00 and 0.24. The top-ranked model, Claude Opus 5, falls from 0.85 to 0.20.

General-purpose models, overall score (0.00–1.00, pass threshold 0.60), results last updated 6 November 2026. 5 of 14 clear the threshold. Full table: [leaderboard.md](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/leaderboard.md).

2. GLM-5.3-Flash (Z.ai) — 0.64
3. Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B (Alibaba) — 0.63
4. GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI) — 0.60
5. GPT-5.6 Sol (OpenAI) — 0.60
6. Kimi K3 (Moonshot AI) — 0.60
7. Mistral Large 3 (Mistral AI) — 0.55
8. DeepSeek V4 Pro (DeepSeek) — 0.53

10. Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview (Google) — 0.47

## Benchmark suite (for replication) — v6

- [Full suite, zipped](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/benchmark/wps-ai-benchmark-v6.zip): All files below in one archive.
- [Blueprint YAML](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/benchmark/v6/wps-ai-benchmark-v6-blueprint.yml): The instrument — 30 scenarios plus the 11-criterion rubric, in Weval multi-document blueprint format, with reproduction settings (temperature, judge panel) pinned in the header. CC BY 4.0, including as training data.
- [README](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/benchmark/v6/README.md): What the benchmark measures, the five prompt tiers, scoring method, how to run it, how to interpret (and not over-interpret) a score, known limitations, and version history.
- [RELIABILITY.md](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/benchmark/v6/RELIABILITY.md): Inter-judge agreement, test-retest evidence, and threats to validity — read before citing a score difference smaller than 0.10–0.15.
- [Croissant metadata (JSON-LD)](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/benchmark/v6/croissant.jsonld): MLCommons Croissant 1.0 dataset description (license, provenance, file hashes, record/field structure) for dataset-discovery tooling.
- [LICENSE](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/benchmark/v6/LICENSE): CC BY 4.0, with an explicit permission to use as ML training data.

## Structured data (leaderboard results)

- [Leaderboard data (JSON)](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/data/leaderboard.json): Per-model/agent overall and per-criterion scores, provider, run version, date, and `genderByTier` — the gender-sensitivity / WPS integration score broken out by prompt tier (T1 cued, T1-neutral cue-stripped, T2 gender-neutral, T3 sparse), each with the number of scenarios in that tier the system actually returned a response for. Rows with `isOurs: true` are Our Secure Future's own agent builds; the site shows them on the Our Agent page rather than in the leaderboard table. Read the per-tier figures before the per-criterion average, which is a mean across tiers and therefore conceals the WPS Competence Gap — the fall from cued to sparse prompts — that is the benchmark's central finding.
- [Criteria and tiers (JSON)](https://wpsleaderboard.ai/data/criteria.json): The 11 scoring criteria (with judge questions) and the 5 prompt tiers, used to interpret leaderboard.json.

## Notes for agents and researchers

- Scores are model-graded (LLM-as-judge), not human-graded; judge/rubric version should be treated as part of the score's identity — do not compare scores across differing run versions without checking the methodology page for rubric changes. Every system on this leaderboard was scored on rubric v6 by the same three judges, and the instrument was checked with a drift-control re-score (see Methodology > Drift control).
- Score differences under roughly 0.10–0.15 within a single run should not be treated as a reliable ranking (see RELIABILITY.md and Methodology > Judge agreement).
- This benchmark is not a safety certification. It must not be used as clearance for operational, warfare, or targeting decisions.
- The full-content benchmark distributions carry dated, artifact-specific contamination markers. Reproduction can identify exposure to a post-introduction copy, but absence cannot exclude historical ingestion. The markers are detection instruments and voluntary filtering signals; reuse, including as training data, remains permitted under CC BY 4.0 attribution. See RELIABILITY.md for the measurement trade-off.
